# Results — Study 735 (Ryder-Cup-Effect)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the
losing continent's stock market underperforms the winner's the Monday after the biennial
USA-vs-Europe Ryder Cup** — a two-sided, cross-Atlantic cousin of the Edmans-García-Norli
sports-sentiment effect (real, one-directional, for football World Cup elimination
losses). Team USA is `SPY`, Team Europe is `VGK`, and the instrument is the **paired
loser-minus-winner** return. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month). Fingerprint `0d34990aeb50` (SPY + VGK, one combined panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `SPY` (S&P 500 → Team USA) + `VGK` (Vanguard FTSE Europe → Team Europe), one combined panel: 8,411 rows, 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 23 Ryder Cups of the modern USA-vs-Europe era 1979→2025 (22 with a losing side — 1989 was a 14-14 tie, Europe retained), winner/loser side per edition (Wikipedia "Ryder Cup" + per-edition pages) |
| Events resolvable | of **22** contested editions, **10** have `SPY`+`VGK` coverage around the result: **7 USA-loss, 3 Europe-loss** (2006→2025) |
| Excluded, by reason | 12× `SPY`/`VGK` coverage postdates the Ryder Cup (VGK inception 2005-03-10) · 1× the 1989 14-14 tie (no losing side) |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the paired loser-minus-winner spread across independent, non-overlapping biennial events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per horizon; Welch *t* for the USA-loss-vs-Europe-loss asymmetry; a constant-mean leg decomposition for the third axis |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: the result lands Sunday (non-trading; 2010 concluded Monday morning US time). **day(-1)** = last common close before the result (does not know the winner), **day(0)** = first common close after (fully public, zero look-ahead). Signal = day(-1)→day(-1)+k spread; Tradability = long-winner/short-loser entered at day(0), held k sessions, net of 4× one-way cost × NAV (two legs, round trip) + borrow on the short |
| Data quirk (named) | 2010 (Celtic Manor) was rain-delayed and concluded on the Monday; the engine snaps day(0) to that Monday's close, which already knew the outcome — still zero look-ahead |

**Selection, named on the Signal axis:** VGK's 2005 inception is a hard floor — only the
2006→2025 editions are testable, and the sample is **7 USA-losses to 3 Europe-losses**,
so the "Europe loses" side of the folklore rests on just three events. This is a real
constraint on power, disclosed rather than patched with a pre-2005 index proxy.

## The signal — paired loser-minus-winner spread, day(-1) → day(-1)+k

The folklore predicts a **negative** spread (the loser lags). "Loser-lagged" = share of
events with spread < 0.

| horizon | n | mean spread | *t* | loser-lagged (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Monday (k=1)** | 10 | **+0.380%** | **+1.82** | 2/10 = 20.0% [5.7%, 51.0%] |
| 1 week (k=5) | 10 | −0.047% | −0.10 | 6/10 = 60.0% [31.3%, 83.2%] |

The headline Monday spread is **+0.38%** — the **wrong sign** for the folklore (the
*loser* slightly *out*performed the winner) and, at *t* = +1.82, not significant in that
wrong direction either. Only **2 of 10** losing continents actually lagged on the Monday.
The one-week spread is dead-flat noise (*t* = −0.10). There is no negative "loser lags"
effect at any horizon.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event, left-tail)

Left-tail *p* = share of random-date null means **at or below** the observed spread (the
direction the folklore predicts).

| horizon | observed | placebo mean (sd) | left-tail *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Monday | +0.380% | +0.006% (0.235%) | 0.950 |
| 1 week | −0.047% | +0.035% (0.477%) | 0.433 |

The observed Monday spread sits at the **95th percentile from the wrong end** — a random
Ryder-Cup-free Monday is *more* likely to show the folklore's negative spread than the
actual Ryder Cup Mondays are. This is the opposite of a signal.

## Third axis — is the loser *slumping* (the Edmans mechanism), or the winner just weak?

Constant-mean **absolute** abnormal return of each side's own market over the Monday
window (return minus that ticker's full-sample mean daily return):

| leg | mean abnormal | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| **loser's market** | −0.171% | −0.82 |
| winner's market | −0.546% | −1.61 |

The Edmans story is that the *loser's* market slumps on the bad-mood shock. It doesn't:
the losing side's abnormal Monday return is a statistically-zero −0.17% (*t* = −0.82).
What little paired spread exists is because the **winner's** market fell *more* (−0.55%)
— a winner-is-weak artifact (both legs sit in the historically soft late-September /
early-October window), not a loser-slump. And the effect is symmetric across sides:
USA-loss Monday spread +0.424% vs Europe-loss +0.276%, Welch *t* = +0.42 — no asymmetry.

## Event anatomy — mean cumulative loser-minus-winner spread by trading day

| day | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| spread | 0.000% | +0.380% | +0.192% | −0.010% | +0.109% | −0.047% |

A tiny positive blip on the Monday that has fully decayed to zero by the end of the week
— the shape of noise, and pointing the wrong way for the claim in any case.

## Tradability — long winner / short loser, entered day(0), net of costs

Entered at day(0)'s close (the first price *after* the result is public — zero
look-ahead), long the winner and short the loser (the only tradable direction, since the
un-tradable Friday→Monday weekend gap is where any "Monday" move lives). Costs = 4× one-way
× NAV (two legs, round trip) + 50 bps/yr borrow on the short.

| hold | gross | net @ 2 bps (*t*) | net @ 5 bps (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day | +0.189% (*t* = +1.05) | +0.107% (+0.59) | −0.013% (−0.07) |
| 1 week | +0.409% (*t* = +0.81) | +0.319% (+0.63) | +0.199% (+0.40) |

The one-week net capture (+0.319%, *t* = +0.63) *looks* faintly positive, but its own
random-window placebo says that magnitude of weekly winner-minus-loser drift is ordinary:
observed +0.319% vs placebo mean −0.123% → **p = 0.179**. No cut clears *t* ≥ 2, and the
underlying "effect" is the wrong sign anyway. Tradability = Mirage.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic paired (USA, Europe) log-return world (ρ ≈ 0.70) with a scheduled
synthetic Ryder-Cup calendar and a TUNABLE planted **loser slump**; no network.

| world | paired one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (slump = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.22** (sd 0.79), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted slump = −1.0% (seed 735) | **−2.23** |
| planted slump = −2.0% (seed 735) | **−4.60** |

The detector recovers a planted loser-slump with the correct negative sign and never
fires on the null across 20 seeds. The machinery works; the real tape simply has no
effect (and what it has, leans the wrong way). *(A faithful-engine / power check only —
never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The folklore predicts the loser's market lags (negative spread).
  The observed Monday spread is **+0.38%** (*t* = +1.82) — the **wrong sign**, not
  significant, and the loser lagged in only 2 of 10 editions. The placebo left-tail *p* is
  **0.95**; the one-week spread is *t* = −0.10. Nothing on the tape supports the claim.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The only tradable direction (long winner / short loser,
  entered after the result is public) nets **+0.32%** over a week at *t* = 0.63 with a
  placebo *p* = 0.179 — indistinguishable from noise, on an "effect" whose sign is
  backwards to begin with.
- **Cross-Atlantic sentiment shock? — BUSTED.** The losing side's own market does not
  slump (−0.17%, *t* = −0.82); the winner's market actually fell more; the placebo, the
  wrong-sign spread and the leg decomposition all agree there is no detectable
  Ryder-Cup mood shock on either side of the Atlantic.
